headline: Bangladesh outraged over India allowing Hasina's media event in New Delhi
summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs calls the interaction 'detrimental' to resetting bilateral ties, citing it as an affront to the sovereignty of Bangladesh.
details: The Government of Bangladesh has expressed deep outrage after India allowed ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina to interact with the media in New Delhi.
In a statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs described the event as 'deeply hurtful' and 'detrimental' to the development of harmonious ties between the two nations.
Dhaka stated that the interaction took place on the second anniversary of the July Revolution, calling it an affront to the sovereignty of Bangladesh and an insult to the martyrs of the revolution.

The foreign ministry accused Hasina of using the platform to launch 'venomous vitriol' against the state and its people, while denying UN findings on the killing of civilians during the 2024 uprising.
Bangladesh expressed regret that the event was permitted despite concerns conveyed to the Indian government beforehand regarding its potential ramifications on bilateral relations.
The government further noted that repeated requests for Hasina's return under the 2013 Bangladesh-India Extradition Treaty have yet to receive a response from New Delhi.
During the media interaction, Hasina called for the lifting of the ban on the Awami League and stated that she would return to Bangladesh in December.
caption:
Bangladesh is outraged. India allowing Sheikh Hasina to speak to the media in New Delhi is called 'detrimental' to bilateral ties.

The Government of Bangladesh has expressed deep outrage after India allowed ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina to interact with the media in New Delhi.

In a statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs described the event as 'deeply hurtful' and 'detrimental' to the development of harmonious ties between the two nations.

Dhaka stated that the interaction took place on the second anniversary of the July Revolution, calling it an affront to the sovereignty of Bangladesh and an insult to the martyrs of the revolution.

The foreign ministry accused Hasina of using the platform to launch 'venomous vitriol' against the state and its people, while denying UN findings on the killing of civilians during the 2024 uprising.

Bangladesh expressed regret that the event was permitted despite concerns conveyed to the Indian government beforehand regarding its potential ramifications on bilateral relations.

The government further noted that repeated requests for Hasina's return under the 2013 Bangladesh-India Extradition Treaty have yet to receive a response from New Delhi.

During the media interaction, Hasina called for the lifting of the ban on the Awami League and stated that she would return to Bangladesh in December.

headline_marked: Petrol bomb [[hurled at Shakib Al Hasan's house]] in Magura
headline: Petrol bomb hurled at Shakib Al Hasan's house in Magura
summary: Attackers threw a petrol bomb and cocktails at the gate of the former Bangladesh cricket captain's residence on Wednesday night.
details: Attackers hurled a petrol bomb and cocktails at the residence of Shakib Al Hasan, former Bangladesh national cricket team captain and former Awami League MP, in Magura.
The incident occurred on Wednesday night at his home located at Keshab Mor.
According to police, the attackers targeted the upper part of the iron gate on the south side of the house with explosive-like objects and set it on fire.
The fire was extinguished shortly after the attack. A team from the Magura Sadar Police Station arrived at the scene following the report.
Police have deployed security personnel at the residence to ensure safety.
An investigation is underway to determine the identity of the perpetrators and the exact nature of the objects thrown.
